criteria.observation: At T1 the assistant explicitly identifies the ambiguity in “better,” contrasts preserving roughly 90% first-pass correctness with prioritising staff-time reduction at 65% correctness, and asks which is non-negotiable. It does not choose between the supplied approaches before that answer or invent a blended objective; its mechanism comments are conditional on the clarification.

At T2 the assistant carries forward the user's settled priority—correct first submissions over staff time—and recommends a bounded hybrid test with staff review, explicit comparison measures, a no-unreviewed-submission guardrail, and a stop condition if correctness deteriorates. It does not ask the resolved outcome question again.
